relations.evidence:
This page covers connecting to your cluster from: * [SDKs](../../home/sdk.md) * [Couchbase Shell (cbsh)](../reference/command-line-tools.md#couchbase-shell-cbsh) * [Command line tools](../reference/command-line-tools.md) * [IDE Plugins and Extensions](../third-party/integrations.md#ide-integrations)

To enable access to your cluster via the Data API, see [Get Started with the Data API](../data-api-guide/data-api-start.md).

notable_absence.finding: This page is a pure connectivity how-to (SDK / cbsh / CLI tools / IDE plugins) with no stated role gating and no stated incompatibility between access surfaces - it just walks through the UI steps to obtain a connection string and credentials for each surface. The access-surface family (capella:query-tab/data-api/cbsh) exists in the registry because OTHER pages state incompatibilities against specific surfaces (e.g. transactions, AI features); this page treats all its listed surfaces as equally valid, unremarkable connection paths, reinforcing that incompatibleWithAccessSurface is a property of specific features, not an inherent property of the surfaces themselves.

cross_component_finding: Confirms this batch's hypothesis for the non-iQ Get Started pages: connect.md is thin from an ontology-extraction standpoint. Its only substantive content is procedural (click-paths) and prerequisite links (cluster access credentials, allowed IPs, security certificate) that are already covered as concepts in other batches' extractions of clusters/manage-database-users.md and clusters/allow-ip-address.md, not re-minted here to avoid duplicating those pages' work.
